A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic CHD risk score was a valid measure of genetic CHD risk in this population of subjects with type 1 diabetes.
the genetic risk score did not differ between groups and that the genetic risk did not add to clinical risk.
the 19 SNPs in the array are not associated with CHD risk in T2D subjects, and that this is not due to a failure of the genotyping assay.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 19-SNP GS does not differ in this T2D cohort compared with the general population, and is associated with LDL- and family history in the healthy population, suggesting the 19-SNPs are not specific to T2D subjects, and that the GS could be a useful addition to the current CHD risk prediction models in T2D.
we can accurately genotype the 19 SNPs using the Randox Cardiac Risk Array, which will allow us to determine the genetic risk score for CHD.
